record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: Generalize the tetrachoric-series approach for the bivariate Gaussian copula to the n-variate Gaussian-copula setting for n ≥ 3, and formulate the corresponding version of the χ_p-realization problem: whether the resulting multivariate copula-based correlation functions arise from suitable sign-valued functions in the workflow for Grothendieck-type bounds.

evidence.quote: (2-RP2) Generalise the above approach (which is built on the tetrachoric series of the bivariate Gaussian copula) to the n-variate case, where n ∈ N3 and adapt problem (2-RP1) accordingly.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) Bivariate Gaussian copula and tetrachoric series. Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be a centered Gaussian vector with $\mathbb{E}[X_i^2]=1$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_1 X_2]=\rho\in[-1,1]$. For real-valued square-integrable functions $f,g$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with respect to the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma$, expand $f=\sum_{k\ge 0}\hat f_k H_k$ and $g=\sum_{k\ge 0}\hat g_k H_k$ in the orthonormal Hermite basis $\{H_k\}_{k\ge 0}$. The Mehler/tetrachoric identity gives
$$\mathbb{E}[f(X_1)g(X_2)]=\sum_{k\ge 0}\hat f_k\,\hat g_k\,\rho^{k}.$$
For sign-valued $f,g\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,+1\}$ define
$$T_{f,g}(\rho):=\mathbb{E}[f(X_1)g(X_2)],$$
which is an odd-or-even real-analytic function of $\rho$ on $[-1,1]$ with $T_{f,g}(\pm 1)\in[-1,1]$.

(b) The bivariate $\chi_p$-realization problem. For a fixed exponent $p\ge 1$, the bivariate $\chi_p$-realization problem asks: which functions $\varphi\colon[-1,1]\to[-1,1]$ admit a representation
$$\varphi(\rho)=\mathbb{E}[f(X_1)g(X_2)]$$
for some pair of measurable sign-valued functions $f,g\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,+1\}$, possibly subject to $L^p$-type normalizations on the Hermite coefficients? Equivalently, which kernels $\varphi$ on $[-1,1]$ arise as completely correlation preserving (CCP) functions through Gaussian rounding, in the workflow used to derive Grothendieck-type bounds?

Problem. Let $n\ge 3$ be an integer. Let $\mathbf X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ be a centered Gaussian vector with unit variances and correlation matrix $R=(\rho_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}\in\mathcal{C}_n$, where $\mathcal{C}_n$ denotes the set of $n\times n$ correlation matrices.

(i) Develop the multivariate analogue of the tetrachoric/Mehler expansion: derive a closed-form Hermite-type series representation, in terms of $R$, of
$$T_{f_1,\dots,f_n}(R):=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{n} f_i(X_i)\right]$$
for arbitrary sign-valued functions $f_i\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,+1\}$, $i=1,\dots,n$, including explicit formulas for the multivariate analogues of the tetrachoric coefficients.

(ii) Formulate and resolve the $n$-variate $\chi_p$-realization problem: characterize, for $n\ge 3$ and $p\ge 1$, the class of functions $\Phi\colon\mathcal{C}_n\to[-1,1]$ that can be realized as
$$\Phi(R)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{n} f_i(X_i)\right]$$
for some choice of sign-valued $f_1,\dots,f_n$, and determine which such $\Phi$ arise as completely correlation preserving functions in the multivariate Gaussian rounding scheme used to obtain Grothendieck-type bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as a research problem (a multivariate generalization of a stated bivariate $\chi_p$-realization problem). Web searches did not reveal a published resolution of either the multivariate tetrachoric/CCP characterization for $n\ge 3$ or the corresponding $\chi_p$-realization problem. It therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Copulae: An overview and recent developments
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of copula theory does not address the multivariate CCP/Grothendieck $\chi_p$-realization question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent copula surveys do not report a solution to a multivariate CCP $\chi_p$-realization problem.

status_evidence.title: Gaussian Copula - ScienceDirect Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Standard treatments of multivariate Gaussian copulas focus on dependence modelling and do not solve the realization-by-sign-valued-functions question.
status_evidence.claim: No standard reference identifies the multivariate $\chi_p$-realization characterization.
